slot.brief: Present a Fischer projection of a molecule with two stereocentres and ask how many R/S configurations and stereoisomers result; test the Fischer-to-R/S rule.

stem:
The following Fischer projection represents 2,3-dibromobutane. What are the configurations at C2 and C3, respectively, and how many stereoisomers does the compound have?
$$\begin{array}{ccc} & \text{CH}_3 & \\ & | & \\ \text{Br} & {-}\text{C}{-} & \text{H} \\ & | & \\ \text{H} & {-}\text{C}{-} & \text{Br} \\ & | & \\ & \text{CH}_3 & \end{array}$$

verdicts.working: At C2, priorities are Br > C3 > CH3 > H; with H on a horizontal bond, reverse the direction to get R. At C3, priorities are Br > C2 > CH3 > H; likewise, reverse to get R. The two equivalent ends give three stereoisomers: RR, SS, and the meso form.

working:
C2 priorities: $\text{Br}>\text{C3}>\text{CH}_3>\text{H}$; lowest priority is horizontal, so invert: $R$.
C3 priorities: $\text{Br}>\text{C2}>\text{CH}_3>\text{H}$; lowest priority is horizontal, so invert: $R$.
The $RR/SS$ pair and one $RS$ meso form give $3$ stereoisomers.

Independent check: At C2, priorities are Br > C3 > CH3 > H; with H on a horizontal bond, reverse the direction to get R. At C3, priorities are Br > C2 > CH3 > H; likewise, reverse to get R. The two equivalent ends give three stereoisomers: RR, SS, and the meso form.
solution: At both C2 and C3, the priorities are $\mathrm{Br>C>CH_3>H}$. Since the lowest-priority group H lies on a horizontal bond in each Fischer projection, reverse the observed order: both centers are $R$. The stereoisomers are the $RR/SS$ pair and one $RS$ meso form, giving $3$ in total.
